newsitem.title: JAPAN: TEPCO nuclear reactor starts commercial operations.
newsitem.headline: TEPCO nuclear reactor starts commercial operations.

text.p: Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) said it started commercial operations of its 1.36 million kw reactor at its Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear power plant in northern Japan on Wednesday morning.
"The reactor successfully completed final inspections by the trade ministry this morning, and started commercial operations immediately," a TEPCO spokesman said.

The new reactor, the plant's seventh, has raised the total power generation capacity of the plant to 8.2 million kw, making the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa complex the world's largest nuclear power plant, surpassing Canada's 7.3-million-kw Bruce plant in Ontario.
A consortium comprising Toshiba Corp, Hitachi Ltd and General Electric Co of the United States built the reactor at a cost of about 360 billion yen, the spokesman said.
